prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell). Airports Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional and Southport keep safety authority. Parts: Demand Prediction Service (Marlinstone); Capacity Assessment Module (CAM; supplies constraints; never originates safety judgments); Slot Allocation Engine (Blueharbor; matches Marlinstone demand to CAM constraints; inputs FIM, Airport Capacity Plan, Airport Acceptance Rate, runway metering limits, sector loading; under GDP derives CTT/arrival opportunity within capacity envelope before local preference); Airport CDM Portal (Foxglove; Common Situation Display; records duty confirmations; publishes slot results); Digital Briefing Room; Tower Sequence Manager; Ramp Movement Board (sends movement updates to Audit Event Ledger); Departure Metering Service; Arrival Regulation Console; Contingency Operations Console; Weather Ingest Gateway (WIG, Orchard); Flight Data Exchange; Surface Surveillance Adapter (apron sensors, evidence only); Airline Interface Adapter (sends advisory operator preferences); Alert Distribution Hub; Performance Analytics Warehouse; Identity Access Service; Business Rules Registry (BRR; fairness rules); Time Synchronization Service; Collaborative Decision Log (resequencing reason, aircraft, parties, approval time); North/South Runway Meter; Sector Load Monitor; Gate Conflict Detector; Handling Resource Planner. Actors: Regional Flow Manager (Copperfin; owns priority policy; may change rules in Capacity Reduction State); Slot Coordinator (runs allocation, reviews exceptions, confirms publication); Airline Operations Coordinator (Saffron); Aircraft Operator Representative; Ground Handling Dispatcher; Ramp Control Lead (Quartzline; sends Stand Tow Request Form; escalates to Tower Supervisor, Airport Duty Manager); Tower Supervisor (Brindle); Airport Duty Manager; Meteorology Briefing Officer; Data Governance Steward; System Support Engineer. Items: TOBT (readiness test), CTT, Tactical Regulation Proposal, GDP status, Storm Cell Snapshot, Runway Inspection Note, Post Operations Report, weather update, duty coordination alert. Modes: Normal Operations; Adverse Weather Mode; Capacity Reduction State; Recovery Phase. Requirements: Orchard shall issue time-stamped weather updates; no pushback until Tower Supervisor confirms; Marlinstone shall refresh stand forecasts on material off-block change; priority order safety/emergency/humanitarian/national, then scheduled, then GA/discretionary; engine shall not excessively delay an operator unless rule basis is visible and logged; unready aircraft may be resequenced.

New part:
S237: The Airline Operations Coordinator uses the delay slip when requesting an exemption review for a crew connectivity constraint that is not already represented in the allocation data.
S238: Exemption requests are evaluated against safety impact, network impact, passenger impact, crew legality, and the availability of a lower-impact alternative.
S239: The Slot Coordinator records each accepted or rejected exemption in the Collaborative Decision Log with the rule applied, the approving role, and the expected operational consequence.
S240: The Data Governance Steward ensures that exemption categories, priority codes, and fairness metrics are versioned in the Business Rules Registry before they are used in live allocation.
S241: The Arrival Regulation Console presents proposed arrival opportunities with the capacity source, regulation start time, and expected delay for each affected flight.
S242: The Departure Metering Service presents proposed departure opportunities and associated Calculated Takeoff Time values for coordination with the Tower Sequence Manager.
S243: The Tower Supervisor may reject a proposed departure opportunity when runway safety, wake spacing, or local sequencing conditions make the proposal impracticable.
S244: The Ramp Control Lead may identify apron constraints through the Ramp Movement Board, but the Slot Allocation Engine remains responsible for recalculating the regulated opportunity.
S245: All allocation runs are time stamped by the Time Synchronization Service and written to the Audit Event Ledger for later reconstruction of the decision sequence.
S246: During Normal Operations, allocation results are refreshed at regular intervals, while Adverse Weather Mode and Recovery Phase allow shorter recalculation cycles approved by the Regional Flow Manager.
S247: If the Regional Flow Platform enters Contingency Fallback State, the Contingency Operations Console preserves the last valid allocation, supports manual amendments, and marks the resulting Slot Compliance State as provisional.
S248: Post-event assessment in the Performance Analytics Warehouse compares proposed opportunities, actual movement times, exemption usage, and operator-level delay equity to improve subsequent rule calibration.
S249: Collaborative target time management establishes a shared operating baseline for each departure by linking the Target Off Block Time, the Calculated Takeoff Time, and the key surface milestone timestamps to the same flight record.
S250: The Regional Flow Platform creates the initial Target Off Block Time proposal from current flight intent, stand readiness, turnaround progress, and applicable airport capacity constraints.
S251: The Demand Prediction Service estimates demand pressure over the next planning horizon and marks flights whose proposed Target Off Block Time values are likely to cause runway or sector imbalance.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
